package_info.package_versions: 26 open-source NetBeans Java projects (various versions, not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: Octopus Scanner is a supply chain malware campaign that injected malicious code into legitimate open-source NetBeans Java projects hosted on GitHub. The malware compromises developer environments by infecting build scripts, propagates itself to other projects and artifacts, steals sensitive information such as credentials and environment variables, and exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling widespread compromise of both developers and downstream users.

execution_context.trigger: build-time (when project is built in NetBeans)
execution_context.file_location: build scripts (e.g., build.xml, project build files) within infected NetBeans projects
required_permissions: filesystem (read/write access to project directories and build scripts)
network (outbound connections for payload download and propagation)
environment_vars (access to environment variables for propagation and infection logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code checks if it is running in a NetBeans environment, recursively modifies build scripts of all projects in the workspace to insert malicious logic, downloads and drops the malware payload into the project output directory, and initiates exfiltration of sensitive data, resulting in the infection of the developer's environment and further propagation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Build scripts are not expected to self-replicate, modify other projects, or perform network operations to download and drop additional payloads. The presence of code that infects other projects and initiates data exfiltration is highly anomalous and indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build scripts automate compilation, testing, and packaging of the current project only. They do not modify unrelated projects, replicate themselves, or perform credential or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build tools may update dependencies or perform static analysis, but do not propagate code to other projects or exfiltrate sensitive data. Any network activity is typically limited to fetching dependencies from trusted repositories.
key_indicators: Recursive modification of build scripts across multiple projects
Network activity to download additional payloads during build
Insertion of obfuscated or hidden code into build.xml or similar files
Initiation of data exfiltration routines from build scripts

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when infected artifact, such as a JAR file, is executed)
execution_context.file_location: malicious payload dropped into project output (e.g., JAR files in build output directories)
required_permissions: filesystem (read access to sensitive files and environment variables)
environment_vars (access to environment variables for credential harvesting)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code embedded in the malicious payload collects developer credentials and environment information from the infected system, then transmits this data via outbound network requests to a remote command-and-control server, resulting in credential theft and potential further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Application code should not access developer credentials or environment variables unrelated to its function, nor should it transmit such data to external servers. The presence of credential harvesting and C2 communication is a clear sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate application code processes user or application data, not developer credentials or environment details. Outbound network communication should be limited to documented, user-initiated actions, not hidden exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Crash reporting or telemetry tools may collect environment information, but only with explicit user consent and never credentials. Such tools also communicate with known, trusted endpoints, not attacker-controlled infrastructure.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive files or environment variables at runtime
Outbound network connections to hardcoded or suspicious C2 domains/IPs
Code within JAR files that performs credential harvesting
Lack of user notification or consent for data collection and transmission

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into open-source NetBeans Java projects' build scripts on GitHub, replacing or modifying files such as build.xml to include infection logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Infection of developer environments when the compromised project is built

attack_chain.action: When a developer builds the infected project, the malicious build script recursively infects all other NetBeans projects in the workspace and downloads/drops the malware payload into the build output.
attack_chain.leads_to: Propagation of malware to additional projects and creation of infected artifacts

attack_chain.action: The malicious payload is included in built artifacts (e.g., JAR files) and is executed when these artifacts are run on developer or user systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of credential harvesting and data exfiltration routines

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the payload collects sensitive information such as credentials and environment variables, then exfiltrates this data to a remote command-and-control server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data and can leverage it for further compromise of affected systems

behavioral_signatures: Build scripts that recursively modify or inject code into other project build files
Unexpected outbound network connections initiated during build or artifact execution
Artifacts (JAR files) containing code for credential harvesting or C2 communication, especially with obfuscated or hidden logic
file_indicators: Modified build.xml or other build scripts containing obfuscated, hidden, or self-replicating code
Unexpected files or payloads (e.g., additional JARs or binaries) dropped in project output directories
JAR files with embedded credential-stealing or network communication code not present in legitimate project versions
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known or suspicious C2 domains or IP addresses during build or artifact execution
Unusual HTTP/S POST requests containing environment or credential data to external servers
Network traffic to domains or IPs not associated with the legitimate project or its dependencies
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor and audit build scripts in open-source projects for unauthorized or unexpected modifications, especially code that replicates itself or downloads additional payloads. Use static and dynamic analysis to inspect built artifacts (e.g., JAR files) for embedded credential harvesting or C2 communication logic. Monitor developer environments and build processes for unexpected outbound network connections, particularly during build or artifact execution. Correlate file, behavioral, and network indicators to identify supply chain compromise and prevent propagation.
